applicabilityBasis.summary: Enosys CDP is marketed as a general dollar-pegged crypto-backed stablecoin minted by borrowers against collateral, and anyone can redeem $1-worth of collateral per CDP through the protocol, subject to fees. That is not the same as an identified legal issuer obligation to pay a fixed monetary value: the reviewed documents provide crypto collateral rather than fiat, and legacy website terms do not establish the CDP obligor. Stablecoin-shaped use makes a categorical non-payment-token exemption inappropriate, so GENIUS applicability is unclear.

genius.notes: The current Enosys footer links July 28, 2022 FLR Finance terms. Their indemnification list names Flare Finance B.V. and FLR Finance Foundation, but does not establish either as the legal issuer of Enosys Loans CDP. IssuerEntity and issuerDomicile remain omitted. CDP redemption returns crypto collateral at dollar-equivalent value, subject to fees; the reviewed documents do not establish an issuer obligation to pay USD 1. Loans documentation says community governance was unavailable at launch. Base live-reserve RPC data is not an independent financial-statement attestation. Optional disclosure booleans remain unset. GENIUS remains pre-effective in the reviewed public implementation sources; the general DASP sales restriction is scheduled for July 18, 2028.

sourcesChecked: Independent 2026-10-07 official-domain search for Bucket Protocol, Enosys, DJED and COTI with GENIUS across OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC, NCUA and Treasury; no exact matching approval, qualification, application or registration announcement located.
negativeEvidenceReview.summary: As of 2026-10-07, no public GENIUS PPSI approval, state qualification, official pending application or registered foreign exception naming Enosys Loans CDP's exact issuer was located in the opened regulator materials and reviewed issuer sources. Public CDP mechanics do not establish a legal issuer obligated to redeem dollars or other fixed monetary value, so applicability remains unclear. This is a bounded negative-evidence finding, not an exhaustive private-application search or a determination of unlawful issuance.
